content.title: Tigers’ Opening Day had everything: a gem, a monster homer and pure ‘magic’
content.text: DETROIT, MI — It’s been 194 days since the Detroit Tigers played their last regular season home game.The last time the team stepped foot onto the field was Sept. 21, 2025 with a 6-2 loss to the Atlanta Braves.But that’s in the past.Today, a new team with many familiar faces — and a few new ones — are ready to put Motor City on their shoulders wearing the Detroit English “D” proudly.It’s April 3, and fans have been itching to get back to warmer temperatures filled with hot dogs, peanuts, beer and, well most of all, baseball.It’s a day that baseball fans live for — opening day.And Tigers fans got a taste of the old days as Brandon Inge threw out the ceremonious first pitch to newly-acquired Justin Verlander. The crowd roared with excitement, and for a moment it felt like everyone was transported back to the 2000s.Opening Day at the Detroit Tigers season-opener against the St. Louis Cardinals on Friday, April 3, 2026 at Comerica Park in Detroit. The Tigers won 4-0.(Jake May | MLive.com)Framber Valdez threw six shutout innings in his Detroit debut as the Tigers topped the St. Louis Cardinals 4-0 on Friday afternoon in the home opener at Comerica Park.The Tigers (3-4) snapped a four-game losing streak. They have two more this weekend against the Cardinals (4-3).Detroit finally broke through offensively in the fourth, snapping a streak of 18 scoreless innings — and 37 of 39 — when Riley Greene doubled and Dillon Dingler followed with a two-run homer off Cardinals starter Michael McGreevy. The drive traveled an estimated 433 feet -- the longest homer of Dingler’s career -- and cleared the bullpen in left-center field.Detroit Tigers pitcher Framber Valdez mentally prepares himself for his first start as he walks onto the field during Opening Day at the Detroit Tigers season-opener against the St. Louis Cardinals on Friday, April 3, 2026 at Comerica Park in Detroit. The Tigers won 4-0.(Jake May | MLive.com)Valdez, making his first start at Comerica Park since signing a three-year, $100-plus million contract in February, threw six scoreless innings and was rarely threatened aside from the error-aided fourth.The afternoon also marked the Detroit debut of top prospect Kevin McGonigle, who arrived after a torrid start to his professional career on the road. McGonigle led off the first inning with a 403-foot flyout to center field — a ball that would have been a home run in 12 major league parks. He is still seeking his first career homer but already has two flyouts measured at more than 400 feet.The announced sellout crowd of 45,008 was Detroit’s largest Opening Day attendance since 2017. The game-time temperature of 70 degrees marked the warmest home opener in the city since April 8, 1991, excluding the 2020 season.Friday was the Tigers’ 27th Opening Day at Comerica Park. They’re 18-9 in home openers and have won 15 of their last 18.Opening Day is as much about the fans, their traditions and love of the game as the players and coaches who compete for the city they love.Hunter Reygaert, 12 of Macomb Township, fiddles with his gold chain and cross that bears Psalm 23 as he tailgates with his family ahead of Opening Day at the Detroit Tigers season-opener against the St. Louis Cardinals on Friday, April 3, 2026 at Comerica Park in Detroit. The Tigers won 4-0.(Jake May | MLive.com)Take Hunter Reygaert for example.The 12-year-old from Macomb Township loves baseball. He has since he was at least 5 years old and watches many games alongside his family, especially his father Scott.This is only his second time living the atmosphere of an opening day.Reygaert plays catcher for his travel baseball team Hitz, and loves the feeling and sound of the crack of a bat when you get a good hit. He loves that same sound when Riley Greene hit his 500th career hit, but his personal favorite player is Kerry Carpenter.“When I get or hit or when the Tigers get a hit, it’s just happiness,” Reyaert said. “It makes you proud of what you’ve been working toward. And Carpenter, he just hits good. He plays good too. ... They’re my home team and I love to watch them play. Go Tigers!”Tiffany Murphy, 43 of Sterling Heights, shows her best impression of a Tiger to match her ultra fan face paint and nails during Opening Day at the Detroit Tigers season-opener against the St. Louis Cardinals on Friday, April 3, 2026 at Comerica Park in Detroit. The Tigers won 4-0.(Jake May | MLive.com)Tiffany Murphy, 43 of Sterling Heights, painted her face fully to look like a tiger to support the team, and even got matching nails done.For her, opening day specifically is more than just baseball, it’s a whole vibe.“When you hear everybody scream, you don’t only hear it but you feel it surge through your whole body,” Murphy said. “It’s unforgettable.”For Joni McLellan, 65 of Novi, the game means everything.Baseball — specifically Tigers baseball — has been rooted in her blood since the day she was born.When she was a young child, she recalls her grandfather John Schmidt would chase as many home games as he could afford. When the Tigers were away, he would walk around with a transistor radio in his shirt pocket and listen to the play by play every time the Tigers would play.For her, Opening Day is a pilgrimage she doesn’t to miss. She even brought a first-timer along, her friend Katherine Gothard, 66 of Canton.Joni McLellan, 65 of Novi, embraces a friend during Opening Day at the Detroit Tigers season-opener against the St. Louis Cardinals on Friday, April 3, 2026 at Comerica Park in Detroit. The Tigers won 4-0.(Jake May | MLive.com)Because, for McLellan, it’s about bringing other people in on Detroit’s best kept secret — Tigers baseball is more than a game. It’s a feeling that is hard to put into words.It’s unbelievable. It’s electric. It’s magnetizing, McLellan and Gothard said exchanging adjectives trying to find the right word.Then, McLellan took a breath, gathered herself and found the right one. She exclaimed it, loud and proud.“It’s magic. It’s literally magical. I’ve been watching this game and this team my whole life,” McLellan said. “I have chill bumps (goosebumps) right now. I love this game and I love our Detroit Tigers.”MLive wins 37 awards in statewide Michigan photojournalism contestPets of the week: James Bond is a handsome, sophisticated gentleman.
